newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: RUGBY UNION-Hurricanes not underestimating NSW-Oliver.
newsitem.headline: RUGBY UNION-Hurricanes not underestimating NSW-Oliver.

text.p: WELLINGTON, May 1 - Hurricanes coach Frank Oliver isn't underestimating lowly Super 12 side New South Wales in the leadup to what he regards as the most important game of the year, NZPA reports.
Wellington, third-equal on the Super 12 table, meet New South Wales at Napier's McLean Park on Friday night.
The match against seventh-equal New South Wales provides Wellington with their best chance of qualifying for the semifinals.
A loss would mean they would have to beat either of the two top teams, Auckland or the ACT Brumbies to qualify.
Oliver hasn't yet given any thought to the impending Auckland game, preferring to concentrate on the NSW match and the Hurricanes onward push for the top four.
"This will be the most important game of the year for us," he said.
Oliver is not underestimating New South Wales and was "very aware" the Hurricanes could be beaten if they didn't perform to their maximum potential.
"I'm very wary of NSW," Oliver said.
"They're playing for a bit of pride and guys in the team are playing for test jerseys."
New South Wales will be bolstered by the return of Phil Kearns, David Campese and Michael Brial from injury.
"They're hard-seasoned bloody professionals," former All Black lock Oliver said.
"They do the right things at the right time so we've just got to try and make sure they don't get any ball, basically."

At yesterday's hour-and-a-half training run at Lindisfarne College, Oliver concentrated on ball retention and tackling -- two aspects of the Hurricanes game he wanted to see improved from last week's match against Otago.
He was pleased with the session.
"We were looking for quality and accuracy and I was aware that the players are a little bit tired, so rest was important too."
Players had most of today off, but worked though a lineout session and then faced a light run under the new lights at McLean Park.
"We'll just walk the corners and have a few kicks," Oliver said.
Oliver and his side are disappointed at the loss of halfback Jon Preston from the side.
Preston tried out his leg at training and quickly pulled the plug on tomorrow's match.
"It's the kind of injury that needs rest to come right and you don't know how it's going to react until you try," Preston said.
"You have to be 100 percent to be playing these days and I couldn't see myself getting to that stage in time.
"I warmed up, it wasn't too bad jogging, but when I tried to open up a bit there was pain. I could only get to around 50 percent and that's not good enough."
Preston's calf muscle injury has now been diagnosed as a partial tear rather than a strain.
His place has been taken by Richard Jarman, with Hawke's Bay's Danny Lee in the reserves. Preston will remain with the team in Napier.
